subproblems.title: Choice of a good cutting level: Helly no-concentration, Fatou-bounded slice values and a.e. good slices at one common level
subproblems.statement: Let ν_j (j ∈ ℕ) be measures on the Borel sets of ℝ and let F_j : ℝ → [0, ∞] (j ∈ ℕ) be functions, each a.e.-measurable for Lebesgue measure L¹. Let Good_j (j ∈ ℕ) be predicates on ℝ (Good : ℕ → ℝ → Prop), let a < b be reals and let Λ ∈ [0, ∞). Assume that for every j: ν_j([a, b]) ≤ Λ, ∫_ℝ F_j dL¹ ≤ Λ (lower Lebesgue integral), and Good_j(t) holds for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ. Then there are s ∈ (a, b), a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and C ∈ [0, ∞) with the following properties: Good_j(s) holds for every j ∈ ℕ; F_{φ(j)}(s) ≤ C for every j ∈ ℕ; and for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is δ > 0 with ν_{φ(j)}([s − δ, s]) ≤ ε for all sufficiently large j.

Source: steps 2–4 of the supplied proof of dor_lmb_fc_localize (the monotone/Helly extraction, Fatou's lemma for the slice masses, and the choice of the level t), stated abstractly. In dor_lmb_fc_localize: ν_j := g_#μ_j is the push-forward under g = dist(·, closure W) of the mass measure μ_j = R_j.measure of T_j, so ν_j([s − η, s]) = μ_j({s − η ≤ g ≤ s}) for every band width η > 0. F_j(t) := M_{W₁}(P_{j,t}), where P_{j,t} are the slices of T_j given by (SL) and W₁ = {g < 5σ/2} ⊂⊂ U is open, σ := δ₀/3 being the scale from the setup step. Good_j(t) is the a.e. clause (2) of (SL) for P_{j,t}, and Λ := sup_j M_{W₁}(T_j). Step 2 of the supplied proof constructs limits G(q) of μ_j({f < q}) on rational q and the countable jump set C of G. That step is supplied here by the sibling helly. Its conclusion at a level s ∉ N, that some band {s − η ≤ g ≤ s} eventually carries little mass along the subsequence, is a sufficient substitute for the property of t ∉ C that step 6 of the supplied proof uses (it is precisely the no-concentration hypothesis of the sibling weak_conv).
Tool: the sibling helly (cmc_fc_gs_helly_no_concentration). Let μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) be Borel measures on ℝ, let a, b ∈ ℝ and let Λ ∈ [0, ∞) with μ_j([a, b]) ≤ Λ for every j. Then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and a countable N ⊆ ℝ such that for every s ∈ (a, b) ∖ N and every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is δ > 0 with μ_{φ(j)}([s − δ, s]) ≤ ε for all sufficiently large j.
Notation: L¹ is Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ, 'a.e.' refers to L¹, and liminf is taken in [0, ∞] as the index tends to ∞.
1. (Helly selection.) Apply helly to the measures ν_j, the reals a, b and Λ; its hypothesis is ν_j([a, b]) ≤ Λ < ∞. This gives a strictly increasing φ₁ : ℕ → ℕ and a countable set N ⊆ ℝ with the following property (H). For every s ∈ (a, b) with s ∉ N and every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there are δ > 0 and J ∈ ℕ with ν_{φ₁(i)}([s − δ, s]) ≤ ε for all i ≥ J.
2. (Fatou along φ₁.) For t ∈ ℝ put h(t) := liminf_{i→∞} F_{φ₁(i)}(t) ∈ [0, ∞]. Each F_{φ₁(i)} is a.e.-measurable, so Fatou's lemma for a.e.-measurable functions (Mathlib lintegral_liminf_le') gives ∫ h dL¹ ≤ liminf_i ∫ F_{φ₁(i)} dL¹. Every term satisfies ∫ F_{φ₁(i)} dL¹ ≤ Λ, so this liminf is ≤ Λ (liminf_le_of_frequently_le'). Hence ∫ h dL¹ ≤ Λ < ∞.
3. (h is finite a.e.) h is a.e.-measurable. Indeed, choose measurable F̃_i equal a.e. to F_{φ₁(i)}. The liminf of the F̃_i is measurable (Measurable.liminf), and it equals h outside the countable union of the exceptional null sets (Mathlib AEMeasurable.liminf). An a.e.-measurable [0, ∞]-valued function with finite integral is finite a.e. (ae_lt_top'). So h(t) < ∞ for a.e. t.
4. (A common full-measure set.) For each j the set {t : Good_j(t) fails} is L¹-null. ℕ is countable, so for a.e. t, Good_j(t) holds for every j simultaneously (ae_all_iff). N is countable and L¹ has no atoms, so L¹(N) = 0 (Set.Countable.measure_zero); that is, t ∉ N for a.e. t (measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem). Let B be the set of t ∈ ℝ at which at least one of the following fails: (i) Good_j(t) for every j; (ii) h(t) < ∞; (iii) t ∉ N. Combining these facts with step 3, L¹(B) = 0.
5. (Choice of s.) Since a < b, L¹((a, b)) = b − a > 0 (Real.volume_Ioo). If (a, b) ⊆ B, then L¹((a, b)) ≤ L¹(B) = 0, a contradiction. Hence there is s ∈ (a, b) with s ∉ B. That is, Good_j(s) holds for every j ∈ ℕ, ℓ := h(s) = liminf_i F_{φ₁(i)}(s) < ∞, and s ∉ N.
6. (Subsequence with bounded values.) Put C := ℓ + 1 ∈ [0, ∞); then ℓ < C. A [0, ∞]-valued sequence is bounded below by 0. So by the definition of liminf (frequently_lt_of_liminf_lt), F_{φ₁(i)}(s) < C for infinitely many i. Therefore (extraction_of_frequently_atTop) there is a strictly increasing φ₂ : ℕ → ℕ with F_{φ₁(φ₂(j))}(s) ≤ C for every j ∈ ℕ.
7. (Conclusion.) Let φ := φ₁ ∘ φ₂; it is strictly increasing as a composition of strictly increasing maps. We have s ∈ (a, b) and C ≠ ∞. Good_j(s) holds for every j (step 5), and F_{φ(j)}(s) ≤ C for every j (step 6). Finally let ε ∈ (0, ∞]. Since s ∈ (a, b) and s ∉ N, (H) gives δ > 0 and J with ν_{φ₁(i)}([s − δ, s]) ≤ ε for all i ≥ J. A strictly increasing φ₂ : ℕ → ℕ satisfies φ₂(j) ≥ j. So for every j ≥ J, i := φ₂(j) ≥ J and ν_{φ(j)}([s − δ, s]) = ν_{φ₁(φ₂(j))}([s − δ, s]) ≤ ε. Thus ν_{φ(j)}([s − δ, s]) ≤ ε for all sufficiently large j. ∎
proof_key_steps: Helly (sibling helly) gives a strictly increasing φ₁ and a countable N such that ν_{φ₁(i)} does not concentrate on [s − δ, s] at any s ∈ (a, b) ∖ N.
Fatou: ∫ liminf_i F_{φ₁(i)} ≤ liminf_i ∫ F_{φ₁(i)} ≤ Λ < ∞. The liminf is a.e.-measurable, hence finite a.e.
For a.e. t: Good_j(t) holds for all j (countable intersection), the liminf is finite, and t ∉ N (N is countable, hence null).
(a, b) has positive Lebesgue measure, so such a level s ∈ (a, b) exists.
liminf < ℓ + 1 =: C gives frequently F_{φ₁(i)}(s) < C, hence a subsequence φ₂ with F_{φ₁(φ₂(j))}(s) ≤ C.

Source: steps 0–3, and the ε = ∞ case of step 8, of the parent-supplied proof of cmc_fc_good_slice. That is Helly's selection argument, which realizes elementarily the compactness/atom-counting ingredient of Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2 ("by 4.5(1),(2) and an argument as in 6.7(2) of Ch. 2"). One harmless adjustment: the countable set D = ℚ ∩ (a, b) itself indexes the Tychonoff product, so neither an enumeration of D nor the hypothesis a < b is needed. If b ≤ a, then (a, b) = ∅ and the final claim is vacuous; the argument runs verbatim with D possibly empty.

1. (Restriction.) For j ∈ ℕ let ν_j := μ_j⌞[a, b], i.e. ν_j(E) = μ_j(E ∩ [a, b]) for Borel E ⊆ ℝ. Then ν_j(ℝ) = μ_j([a, b]) ≤ Λ < ∞. So each ν_j is a finite Borel measure with ν_j(E) ≤ Λ for every Borel E, and ν_j(E) = μ_j(E) for every Borel E ⊆ [a, b].

2. (Helly selection.) Let D := {d ∈ ℚ : a < d < b}, a countable set. For j ∈ ℕ define v_j : D → ℝ by v_j(d) := ν_j([a, d]).toReal. Since 0 ≤ ν_j([a, d]) ≤ ν_j(ℝ) ≤ Λ < ∞ and toReal is monotone on finite values, v_j(d) ∈ [0, Λ.toReal]. Thus every v_j lies in K := Π_{d∈D} [0, Λ.toReal] ⊆ ℝ^D. K is compact by Tychonoff (Mathlib isCompact_univ_pi). ℝ^D is a countable product of second countable spaces, so it is second countable and hence first countable. Therefore (Mathlib IsCompact.tendsto_subseq) there are G ∈ K and a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with v_{φ(j)} → G in ℝ^D. Convergence in the product topology is coordinatewise (Mathlib tendsto_pi_nhds), so
  (2.1) ν_{φ(j)}([a, d]).toReal → G(d) as j → ∞, for every d ∈ D.
From G ∈ K, 0 ≤ G(d) ≤ Λ.toReal for every d ∈ D. If d, d' ∈ D and d ≤ d', then [a, d] ⊆ [a, d'], so ν_j([a, d]).toReal ≤ ν_j([a, d']).toReal for every j (both values are finite). Limits preserve non-strict inequalities, so passing to the limit in (2.1) gives G(d) ≤ G(d').

3. (Limit distribution function.) For t ∈ ℝ let A_t := {0} ∪ {G(d) : d ∈ D, d < t} and G̃(t) := sup A_t. A_t is nonempty and bounded above by Λ.toReal, so G̃(t) is a well-defined real number. If t ≤ t', then A_t ⊆ A_{t'}, hence G̃(t) ≤ G̃(t'). So G̃ : ℝ → ℝ is nondecreasing, and therefore the set
  N := {t ∈ ℝ : G̃ is not continuous at t}
is countable (Mathlib Monotone.countable_not_continuousAt). Moreover:
 (α) if d ∈ D and d < t, then G(d) ∈ A_t, so G(d) ≤ G̃(t);
 (β) if d ∈ D and t < d, then G̃(t) ≤ G(d). Indeed every element of A_t is ≤ G(d): the element 0 satisfies 0 ≤ G(d), and an element G(d') with d' ∈ D, d' < t satisfies d' < d, hence G(d') ≤ G(d) by step 2.

4. (The claim.) We show that φ from step 2 (strictly increasing) and N from step 3 (countable) satisfy the conclusion. Let s ∈ (a, b) with s ∉ N, so G̃ is continuous at s, and let ε ∈ (0, ∞]. If ε = ∞, then δ := 1 > 0 works, since every value of a measure is ≤ ∞. Assume from now on that ε < ∞, and put e := ε.toReal. Then e > 0 because 0 < ε < ∞, and ENNReal.ofReal(e) = ε.

5. (Choice of δ.) By continuity of G̃ at s, choose η₀ > 0 such that |G̃(t) − G̃(s)| < e/2 whenever |t − s| < η₀. Put η := min(η₀/3, (s − a)/3, (b − s)/2). Since s − a > 0 and b − s > 0, η > 0, and 2η < η₀, 2η < s − a and s + η < b. By density of ℚ in ℝ (Mathlib exists_rat_btwn), choose rationals d₁, d₂ with s − 2η < d₁ < s − η and s < d₂ < s + η. Then a < s − 2η < d₁ < s < b and a < s < d₂ < s + η < b, so d₁, d₂ ∈ D and d₁ < s < d₂. By (β) with t = s − 2η < d₁, G̃(s − 2η) ≤ G(d₁). By (α) with d₂ < s + η = t, G(d₂) ≤ G̃(s + η). Since |(s + η) − s| = η < η₀ and |(s − 2η) − s| = 2η < η₀, we have G̃(s + η) < G̃(s) + e/2 and G̃(s − 2η) > G̃(s) − e/2. Consequently
  (5.1) G(d₂) − G(d₁) ≤ G̃(s + η) − G̃(s − 2η) < e.
Set δ := η > 0.

6. (Mass bound for each j.) Fix j. Since a < s − 2η < s − δ and s < b, [s − δ, s] ⊆ [a, b], so μ_j([s − δ, s]) = ν_j([s − δ, s]) by step 1. Further, [s − δ, s] ⊆ [a, d₂] ∖ [a, d₁]: a point x with s − δ ≤ x ≤ s satisfies a < x ≤ s < d₂ and x ≥ s − η > d₁. Since d₁ < d₂, [a, d₁] ⊆ [a, d₂]; as ν_j([a, d₁]) < ∞, additivity gives
  ν_j([a, d₂] ∖ [a, d₁]) = ν_j([a, d₂]) − ν_j([a, d₁]) = ENNReal.ofReal(x_j),

1. (A bound for ω.) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U); ω also denotes the underlying smooth compactly supported form. The coefficient norm is |α| = sqrt(Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(d)})²). It is continuous in α: each evaluation α ↦ α(v) at a fixed tuple v is continuous (continuous_eval_const), and squares, finite sums and sqrt are continuous. So x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous. It has compact support because ω does and |0| = 0 (HasCompactSupport.comp_left). Hence it is bounded (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous). Fix c ∈ ℝ with |ω(x)| ≤ c for all x; then c ≥ |ω(0)| ≥ 0.
2. (Cutoff estimate.) Claim: let ν be a measure on ℝ^P with ν(G) < ∞, and ζ a ν-a.e. strongly measurable d-vector field with |⟨α, ζ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for all α, for ν-a.e. x. Let r ∈ ℝ, and let χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] be continuous with χ = 1 on {g ≤ r} and χ = 0 on {g ≥ s}. Then |∫_G⟨ω, ζ⟩ dν - ∫⟨χω, ζ⟩ dν| ≤ c·ν({r < g < s}). Here ν({r < g < s}) ≤ ν(G) < ∞, and its real value is used.
 Proof of the claim.
 (a) F(x) := ⟨ω(x), ζ(x)⟩ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable: (L, v) ↦ L(v) is jointly continuous (Continuous.clm_apply); x ↦ (ζ(x), ω(x)) is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk, ω continuous); and continuous maps preserve a.e. strong measurability (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable).
 (b) For ν-a.e. x, |F(x)| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ c (hypothesis with α := ω(x), and step 1). Also |χ(x)F(x)| ≤ c, since 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1.
 (c) Since ν(G) < ∞, F and χF are integrable on G (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded).
 (d) ⟨χ(x)ω(x), ζ(x)⟩ = χ(x)F(x) by linearity of ζ(x) (map_smul). χF vanishes outside G, where g ≥ s and so χ = 0. Hence ∫χF dν = ∫_G χF dν (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
 (e) By (c) and linearity, ∫_G F dν - ∫_G χF dν = ∫_G (1 - χ)F dν (integral_sub).
 (f) (1 - χ)F vanishes on G ∖ {r < g < s} = G ∩ {g ≤ r}, where χ = 1. Since {r < g < s} ⊆ G and G is Borel, ∫_G (1 - χ)F dν = ∫_{r<g<s} (1 - χ)F dν (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero).
 (g) |(1 - χ)F| ≤ c ν-a.e., because 0 ≤ 1 - χ ≤ 1 and by (b). Since ν({r < g < s}) ≤ ν(G) < ∞, |∫_{r<g<s} (1 - χ)F dν| ≤ c·ν({r < g < s}) (norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const_ae).
 Combining (d)-(g) proves the claim.
3. Fix ε > 0 and put η := ε/(3(c + 1)) > 0.
4. (Small layer for the limit measure.) For i ∈ ℕ let S_i := {s - 1/(i+1) < g < s}.
 - Each S_i is Borel, since g is continuous.
 - The sequence is decreasing: 1/(k+1) ≤ 1/(i+1) for i ≤ k.
 - μ(S_0) ≤ μ(G) < ∞.
 - ⋂_i S_i = ∅: if g(x) < s, choose i with 1/(i+1) < s - g(x) (exists_nat_one_div_lt), so x ∉ S_i; if g(x) ≥ s, then x ∉ S_0.
 By continuity from above (tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop), μ(S_i) → μ(∅) = 0. So some i has μ(S_i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal η. Put δ₁ := 1/(i+1) > 0; then μ({s - δ₁ < g < s}) ≤ η.
5. (Small layer along the sequence.) Apply (H6) with ε := ENNReal.ofReal η > 0. This gives δ₂ > 0 and N₂ with μ_j({s - δ₂ ≤ g ≤ s}) ≤ η for all j ≥ N₂.
6. (Cutoff.) Let δ' := min(δ₁, δ₂) > 0. The set {g ≤ s - δ'} is closed and contained in the open set {g < s - δ'/2}, which is its own interior. By the smooth Urysohn lemma there is a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with χ = 1 on {g ≤ s - δ'} and χ = 0 outside {g < s - δ'/2}; in particular χ = 0 on {g ≥ s}. (Mathlib: exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior with the model modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℝ^P and n = ∞, followed by contMDiff_iff_contDiff.)
7. (The test form χω.) The form χω : x ↦ χ(x)ω(x) is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul). Its support is contained in that of ω, since ω(x) = 0 implies χ(x)ω(x) = 0. So it has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mono'), and tsupport(χω) ⊆ tsupport(ω) ⊆ U (closure_mono). Hence χω ∈ 𝒟^d(U).
8. By (H5) applied to χω there is N₁ with |T_j(χω) - T(χω)| < η for all j ≥ N₁.
9. (Estimate.) Let j ≥ max(N₁, N₂).
 - By (H4), T'_j(ω) = ∫_G⟨ω, ξ_j⟩ dμ_j and T_j(χω) = ∫⟨χω, ξ_j⟩ dμ_j. Step 2 with ν := μ_j, ζ := ξ_j, r := s - δ' applies, by (H1)-(H3) and step 6. Using δ' ≤ δ₂ and step 5, |T'_j(ω) - T_j(χω)| ≤ c·μ_j({s - δ' < g < s}) ≤ c·μ_j({s - δ₂ ≤ g ≤ s}) ≤ cη.
 - Likewise, step 2 with ν := μ and ζ := ξ, together with δ' ≤ δ₁ and step 4, gives |T'(ω) - T(χω)| ≤ c·μ({s - δ' < g < s}) ≤ c·μ({s - δ₁ < g < s}) ≤ cη.
 The passage from the ENNReal bounds to real bounds uses ENNReal.toReal_le_of_le_ofReal.
10. By the triangle inequality, for all j ≥ max(N₁, N₂), |T'_j(ω) - T'(ω)| ≤ |T'_j(ω) - T_j(χω)| + |T_j(χω) - T(χω)| + |T(χω) - T'(ω)| < cη + η + cη = (2c + 1)η < 3(c + 1)η = ε.
11. Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, T'_j(ω) → T'(ω). Since ω was arbitrary, T'_j ⇀ T' (WeaklyConvergesOn). ∎
